conflicts.fact: Definition of hygroscopic vs deliquescent/efflorescent and classification of NaCl and Na2CO3 hydrate; also washing soda formula/forms
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 defines hygroscopic as absorbing moisture without dissolving and classifies Na2CO3.10H2O as efflorescent (losing water to air). Lesson 6 calls anhydrous Na2CO3 the soda ash and washing soda Na2CO3.10H2O, consistent, but Lesson 6 lists hygroscopicity/deliquescence as salt properties without clash. The main conflict is Lesson 5's own Lake Magadi explanation (crust gains/loses water with humidity but is not efflorescence) versus Lesson 5's predict phase saying crusts form in the dry season and shrink in rain; minor.
Lesson 2 gives pH 9–11 (model uses pH 10); Lesson 3 gives ~10.5 and 'around 10'; Lesson 7 gives 10 to 11. Roughly consistent range, small wording variations.

conflicts.fact: Timing of the Lesson 5 petri-dish setup versus lesson sequence
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 says the petri-dish investigation is set up in a 5-minute extension right after Lesson 4 (24 hours before Lesson 5); Lesson 5 observe phase says dishes were massed and photographed at the end of Lesson 4, fine, but Lesson 4's listed duration is 40 minutes of activities with extensions beyond.

conflicts.fact: Number of lessons/model revisions in the unit
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says the Page 1 sketch will be revised in Lessons 3, 4 and 7 and 'six more times'; Lesson 2 adds Version 2 and Lesson 5 and 6 also revise; Lesson 1 says DQB runs 'next eight lessons' while Lesson 7 'sets up Lesson 8' and Lesson 8 says 'across eight lessons'. Revision schedule differs (Lessons 3,4,7 vs 2–7).

conflicts.fact: What the Lesson 1 model is described as being kept by
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says students keep the sketches in their exercise books; Lesson 4 says the model is handed in to the teacher; Lesson 8 says original Lesson 1 models and prediction sheets were kept by the teacher since Lesson 1.

conflicts.fact: Composition of the sufuria white scale
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 says the scale is calcium carbonate from hard water; Lesson 6 links CaCO3 to the sufuria scale; Lesson 3 and the phenomenon say hard water scale is the 'same category' as trona, while Lesson 7 states trona is sodium carbonate and scale is a different salt. Lesson 4 attributes the sufuria's pitting by lemon but Lesson 3 says aluminium reacts with H+ whereas Lesson 4 uses Mg; no direct conflict.

conflicts.fact: Indicator colour sequence for neutralisation and acid used for carbonate reaction
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 Observed says colour changes purple to red when HCl is added to NaOH, while its Observe phase lists purple through blue, green, yellow to red; Lesson 3 shows antacid raising pH red to yellow-green; sulfuric acid with marble chips (Lesson 4) while CaSO4 is slightly soluble, but Lesson 4 antacid carbonate links to HCl in stomach.
